newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 23.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 23.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CHICAGO - Mattel Inc. will next year shift its $55 million
ad budget for Tyco Toys from D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles, New York, to Foote, Cone & Belding and Oglivy & Mather, Los Angeles,
and Young & Rubicam, New York.
WASHINGTON - Web advertising revenue exploded in the first half of 1997, totalling $217.3 million and rising 256.2 percent over the first half of 1996, says Electronic Advertising &
Marketplace Report, a U.S. biweekly newsletter.
NEW DELHI - Coca-Cola India says it has withdrawn a television commercial featuring bungee jumping after a 10-year-old child died in Calcutta while imitating the commercial.
LISBON - Portugal Telecom selects J. Walter Thompson and Imago-Imagem e Comunicacao to provide advertising and publicity services for the forthcoming privatisation of the telecommunications operator.
LONDON - The London Fire Brigade is soliciting sponsorship deals that could include allowing advertisements on fire engines and fire-fighting equipment.
RABAT - Morocco's advertising industry posted a turnover of 750 million dirhams ($77.3 million) in 1996, the Moroccan Confederation of Businesses says.

CHICAGO - Leo Burnett Worldwide forms joint venture with Kontuur Advertising, Tallinn, Estonia to serve local and international clients. Kontuur/Leo Burnett becomes the 83rd full-service office in Burnett's network.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
NEW YORK - The Time Warner cable system has agreed to carry News Corp's 24-hour Fox news channel, The New York Times says.

LONDON - The UK's Independent Television Commission outlines its plans for handling applications from ITV commercial TV companies to renew their licences. It plans a substantial increase in the proportion of the licence payment based on advertising and sponsorship revenue, recognising what it calls "uncertainties surrounding future revenues" for ITV.
LONDON - British media company Granada Group Plc takes control of its neighbour, Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc.
SEATTLE - Microsoft Corp. has purchased a 10-percent stake in Internet start-up Progressive Networks Inc. in a deal aimed at unifying standards for delivering audio and video.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - British tobacco to insurance group B.A.T Industries says it is buying Mexico's largest cigarette maker for $1.7 billion in a move that will dramatically increase its presence in Latin America's lucrative markets.
PURCHASE, New York - PepsiCo Inc says second quarter North American beverage volumes are lower than expected due to relatively cold weather amid intense competition.
BRUSSELS - The European Commission clears new licensing agreements awarded by video-game company Nintendo to firms that develop games for use on its Entertainment System consoles.
TOKYO - Toyota Motor Corp says it hopes to launch hybrid cars, powered by a small engine and an electric motor, in the U.S. and Europe as soon as possible after their launch in Japan,
due by the end of this year.

PARIS - Euro Disney, the operator of the Disneyland Paris theme park, says operating revenues in the April-June quarter rose eight percent to 1.54 billion francs ($251.1 million), helped by a rise in attendance.
PARIS - French food group Danone says it has teamed up with Turkish group Sabanci to create a 50-50 joint venture to produce branded bottled water in Turkey.

LONDON - British cider maker Matthew Clark Plc, whose share price more than halved is "putting robust marketing and commercial plans in place to stabilise our cider business and return it to growth over the medium and long term," says a
spokesman.
LONDON - British supermarket chain J. Sainsbury Plc is teaming up with mutual insurer Standard Life, to offer mortgages along with groceries, the Daily Telegraph newspaper says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TOKYO - A boom in anti-bacterial goods is sweeping Japan as a sweltering summer revives fears of another outbreak of the lethal E.coli bacteria that killed 11 people last year. A mind-boggling array of germ-resistant goods -- including lamps, sprays, memo pads, earphones, portable phones, electric pianos, clothes dryers and baseball mitts -- have started appearing on shop shelves as businesses seek to cash in on the health
worries.

MOSCOW - The world's biggest sell-off is underway in Russia as experienced privatisers auction companies worth billions of dollars. Stakes in leading Russian communications firms, the metals and oil industry, are all up for grabs, say observers.
BEIJING - To deal with the rising number of drug addicts in China's capital city, the government has opened a drug rehabilitation centre on the outskirts of Beijing, the China
Daily says.
